_metadata.description: P0 operational targets for the owner notification spine. Amended 2026-08-17 to make sensitivity labelling default-deny, to name the missing push-provider resource, and to add unroutable visibility, request idempotency, and bounded delivery history.

requirements.title: Real delivery to a personal device
requirements.description: The system shall deliver a notification to the owner's registered iPhone through Web Push from the installed progressive web app, and shall record a delivery receipt for it. The delivery shall not depend on any Vrooli resource, and the notification body shall be encrypted so that no push service can read it.

validation.notes: Requires operator-owned arrival proof on a real registered iPhone; local Web Push encryption and receipt tests are implemented.

requirements.title: Direct notification request
requirements.description: When an agent, scenario, or operator submits a notification request, the system shall persist it and shall return a durable notification id.

validation.notes: Durable acceptance and idempotency are covered by the hub service test.

requirements.title: Device and channel registry
requirements.description: The system shall record the owner's devices, the channels each device accepts, and the address used for each channel.

validation.notes: Device, push address, and quiet-window persistence are covered by the hub service test.

requirements.title: Observable delivery state
requirements.description: The system shall record every delivery attempt with its outcome and shall expose the state of any notification through the API, the CLI, and the UI.

validation.notes: Attempt rows, terminal state, and receipts are covered by the retry/receipt service test; API, CLI, and UI are exercised by their suites.

requirements.title: Quiet hours
requirements.description: When a notification falls inside a configured quiet window, the system shall hold it until the window closes unless its urgency is marked critical.

validation.notes: Quiet-hour hold behavior is covered by the hub service test.

requirements.title: Duplicate suppression
requirements.description: When repeated requests carry the same dedupe key inside its window, the system shall collapse them into one delivery.

validation.notes: Dedupe suppression is covered by the hub service test.

requirements.title: Identity without local accounts
requirements.description: The system shall resolve identity from scenario-authenticator tokens and shall key recipients by that identity, so no password, profile table, or scenario-issued API key exists here.

validation.notes: Identity verification fails closed through the shared owneridentity seam.

requirements.title: Retry with terminal failure
requirements.description: When a delivery attempt fails retryably, the system shall retry with backoff, and shall mark the delivery failed with a stated reason once the retry budget is spent.

validation.notes: Retry backoff and delivery-attempt recording are covered by the hub service test.

requirements.title: Runs without Docker
requirements.description: The system shall declare no resource dependency that requires Docker, so the same build runs on a Linux host and on a macOS fleet node.

validation.notes: The service manifest declares no resource dependency; lifecycle and portability checks are owned by the comprehensive scenario suite.

requirements.title: Sensitivity labelling with default-deny
requirements.description: The system shall require a sensitivity label on every notification at the ingress contract, and shall treat a channel as unapproved for a label unless that channel declares approval. When a channel is unapproved for a notification's label, the system shall deliver a content-free pointer to the console instead of the body, and shall never omit the notification silently.

validation.notes: Sensitivity approval and content-free pointer fallback are covered by the hub routing test.

requirements.title: Unroutable delivery is visible
requirements.description: When no approved channel and no reachable node can serve a notification, the system shall mark it unroutable with a stated reason and shall surface it in the API, the CLI, and the UI. It shall never leave such a notification in a pending state, because a silently pending notification is indistinguishable from one that was never requested.

validation.notes: No-channel requests reach the visible unroutable terminal state.

requirements.title: Request idempotency
requirements.description: When a caller retries a notification request carrying the same idempotency key, the system shall return the original notification id and shall not create a second notification. This is distinct from duplicate suppression: it protects a caller whose request timed out in flight, regardless of any dedupe window.

validation.notes: Repeated requests return the original durable identifier.

requirements.title: Bounded delivery history
requirements.description: The system shall enforce a stated retention rule on notification and delivery-attempt records, and shall record that rule in the data documentation. Retry multiplies attempt rows, so an unbounded history is a defect rather than a deferred feature.

validation.notes: Retention deletion is covered by the hub service test and the retention rule is documented in DATA.md.

requirements.title: Push subscription lifecycle
requirements.description: The system shall store one push subscription per browser and per recipient, shall remove a subscription when the push service reports it gone, and shall renew a subscription when the browser reports it changed. A subscription that expired without replacement shall make the recipient's push channel report unavailable rather than appear healthy.

validation.notes: Subscription replacement and gone-endpoint removal are covered by the push lifecycle service test; real browser renewal remains device validation.

requirements.title: Stable public origin
requirements.description: The scenario shall hold a core-tier public hostname so its origin never expires, because a push subscription is bound to an origin and dies with it. The scenario shall report push as unavailable, with a stated reason, when its origin is not reachable.

validation.notes: Requires operator confirmation that the installed public origin is stable and reachable through tunnel-manager.
